title: Instruction List: counting pulses with a CTU
summary: Call a CTU counter from Instruction List to count three discrete pulses, read its output with LD and reset the count.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real sensor bounces or what a real input does with a pulse shorter than a scan.
objectives: Call a CTU instance with CAL on every scan, passing its inputs, and read its output after the call.
Count the rising edges of PulseInput up to a preset of 3, and clear the count with Reset.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/EdgeCounter.il the counter Count (CTU) is declared but never called, and the program stores FALSE in CountReached. Make CountReached turn ON at the third rising edge of PulseInput and stay ON until Reset clears the count.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which instruction runs a function block in IL, and what CountReached must do at each pulse and at Reset.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario gives PulseInput three pulses, rising at {{t:10}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:50}} ms, and presses Reset at {{t:70}} ms. Predict CountReached at {{t:0}}, {{t:10}}, {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: CountReached stays OFF at {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@0|0}}, {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@10|10}} and {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@30|30}} ms; turns ON at {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=true@50|50}} after the third edge; returns OFF at {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@70|70}} with Reset.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program stores FALSE in CountReached and never calls the counter, so CountReached stays OFF after the third pulse. Change it so that CountReached turns ON at the third rising edge of PulseInput and Reset turns it OFF again. Write the instructions yourself: the declaration is already there.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named EdgeCounter and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow PulseInput and CountReached in the trace: nothing changes on the first two pulses, CountReached rises with the third at {{t:50}} ms, and it falls when Reset rises at {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: CountReached rises once, at the third rising edge, and falls once, with Reset.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Move the line that reads the output of Count above the CAL, so that the output is read before the counter runs. What changes, and in which scan?
stages.checkpoint: The output would show the count of the previous scan, one scan late. In IL the order of the lines is the order in which they run.

hints.text: Look at the line that stores FALSE in CountReached: nothing in it comes from Count, which never runs. A CTU already counts only the rising edges of CU, so a long pulse counts once.
CAL Count(CU := PulseInput, R := Reset, PV := 3), then LD Count.Q and ST CountReached.

faultCases: The starting program stores FALSE in CountReached and never calls the counter, so CountReached stays OFF after the third pulse.
